propositions.text: I dismiss this appeal for the reasons that follow.
propositions.quote: I dismiss this appeal for the reasons that follow.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses this appeal for the reasons that follow.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX is an Indian citizen alleging risk of honour killing by his former fiancée's brother.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX alleged that he is at risk of being the victim of an honour killing by the brother of his former fiancée.

propositions.text: He dated his former fiancée starting in 2013; parents initially opposed but later accepted.
propositions.quote: He began dating his former fiancée in XXXX 2013. Initially, her parents did not support their union but eventually came to accept it.

propositions.text: Engaged in 2014; brother returned angry, threatened and beat Mr. XXXX.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX and his former fiancée became engaged in XXXX 2014 but just over a year later the brother of the fiancée returned from Dubai and became angry at the engagement. He threatened and severely beat Mr. XXXX.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX filed police complaint; families settled amicably; he did not see fiancée again.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX filed a complaint against his fiancée's brother with the police who urged the families to settle amicably, which they did. Following the settlement, Mr. XXXX did not see his fiancée again.

propositions.text: Brother continued threats; police refused help; police raided and arrested Mr. XXXX falsely accusing him.
propositions.quote: The brother continued to threaten Mr. XXXX and the police refused to help. The police raided Mr. XXXX home in XXXX 2015 and arrested him. They falsely accused him of associating with XXXX and XXXX him.

propositions.text: Released after bribe with conditions to stay away from fiancée's family.
propositions.quote: They released him upon the payment of a bribe on certain conditions and told him to stay away from his fiancée's family.

propositions.text: After release, assisted by sister and agent to come to Canada in 2015; tried US visa unsuccessfully; claimed refugee status in 2017.
propositions.quote: When Mr. XXXX was released, his sister who lives in Canada as well as an agent assisted him to come to this country in XXXX 2015. He unsuccessfully tried to obtain a visa to the United States and, when he had difficulty extending his visa to Canada, he claimed refugee status in XXXX 2017.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges risk of honour killing by fiancée's brother, details threats, police harassment, and his refugee claim in Canada.

propositions.text: RPD found Mr. XXXX credible about relationship, threats, beating, and police false accusations.
propositions.quote: The Refugee Protection Division (RPD) found that Mr. XXXX was credible about his relationship with his former fiancée as well as the threats and beating he received from her brother.

propositions.text: RPD accepted credibility of police harassment of parents and brother's accusations in 2016.
propositions.quote: The RPD also appeared to accept as credible that the Punjab police falsely accused Mr. XXXX of associating with XXXXs that they continued to harass his parents who pay them to be left alone, and that the brother of Mr. XXXX former fiancée saw his parents in XXXX 2016 and alleged to them that Mr. XXXX had XXXX the former fiancée.

propositions.text: RPD found Mr. XXXX had viable internal flight alternative in New Delhi, Mumbai, and Calcutta.
propositions.quote: However, the RPD found that Mr. XXXX had a viable internal flight alternative in New Delhi, Mumbai and Calcutta.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found Mr. XXXX credible but concluded he had a viable internal flight alternative in major Indian cities.

propositions.text: RAD denied appeal, upheld RPD's finding of viable internal flight alternative in New Delhi, Mumbai, Calcutta.
propositions.quote: The RAD denied his appeal and upheld the RPD's finding that Mr. XXXX had a viable internal flight alternative in New Delhi, Mumbai and Calcutta.

propositions.text: RAD found no extreme criminal case and no police interest to search outside village or other states.
propositions.quote: In particular, the RAD found that Mr. XXXX did not present an extreme criminal case and that he had not established that the police in his village were interested enough to search for him outside of the village, let alone in other states.

propositions.text: RAD found no evidence police in internal flight cities would contact Punjab police.
propositions.quote: The RAD also found that Mr. XXXX had not established that the police in New Delhi, Mumbai or Calcutta who would take his tenant registration would be in contact with the Punjab police.

propositions.text: RAD found no evidence brother would search for Mr. XXXX in other parts of India; parents endorsed engagement and assured brother would get over anger.
propositions.quote: With respect to Mr. XXXX fear of his former fiancée's brother, the RAD found that he failed to establish that the brother would go out of his way to search for him in other parts of India especially given that Mr. XXXX engagement to his fiancée had been publicly endorsed by her parents and they assured him that the brother would eventually get over his anger.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD upheld the RPD's decision, finding no extreme criminal case or police/brother interest beyond local area.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX sought judicial review of RAD decision.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX then sought judicial review of the RAD's decision.

propositions.text: Federal Court granted judicial review, set aside RAD decision due to three errors undermining reasonableness.
propositions.quote: The Federal Court granted judicial review and set aside the RAD's decision. The Court found that three errors undermined the reasonableness of the RAD's decision.

propositions.text: First, RAD wrongly suggested charges against Mr. XXXX were not serious; charges were among most serious.
propositions.quote: First, the Court held that, even if it may be the case that interstate communications between police forces are limited to serious charges, it was wrong for the RAD to suggest that the charges made against Mr. XXXX in this case were not serious. According to the Court, the brother of Mr. XXXX ex-fiancée accused Mr. XXXX of being a XXXX and of XXXX the ex-fiancée which, the Court noted, are among the most serious of charges.

propositions.text: Second, given brother's police contacts and police targeting, unreasonable not to conclude brother pressured police to locate Mr. XXXX.
propositions.quote: Second, given the evidence that the brother of Mr. XXXX ex-fiancée had contacts within the police and the police's targeting of Mr. XXXX, it was unreasonable not to conclude that the brother was using his contacts with the police to pressure them to locate Mr. XXXX.

propositions.text: Third, speculative for RAD to find brother would accept relationship due to parents' public approval.
propositions.quote: Third, the Court found that it was speculative of the RAD to find that the brother would eventually accept Mr. XXXX relations with his ex-fiancée because her parents had publicly approved of their union.

propositions.text: Court found RAD failed to provide transparent, intelligible, reasonable analysis; referred matter back to RAD for reconsideration.
propositions.quote: Due to these errors, the Court found that the RAD failed to provide a transparent, intelligible, and reasonable analysis and referred the matter back to the RAD for reconsideration.

paragraphs.summary: The Federal Court granted judicial review, found three errors in RAD's decision, and referred matter back for reconsideration.

propositions.text: My role is to review all evidence, including RPD hearing recording, and decide correctness of RPD decision.
propositions.quote: My role is to look at all the evidence, including the recording of the RPD hearing, and decide if the RPD made the correct decision in light of the evidence in the case, the Federal Court's decision on judicial review, and all other relevant case law.

propositions.text: RPD erred relying on former fiancée's parents' opinion that brother would accept relationship.
propositions.quote: Having carefully reviewed all of the evidence and submissions in this case, including the audio-recording of the RPD hearing, I find that the RPD erred in relying upon the opinion of the former fiancée's parents that the brother would eventually accept Mr. XXXX relationship with his former fiancée.

propositions.text: RPD and first RAD member failed to provide fulsome review of evidence supporting their conclusions.
propositions.quote: I also find that the RPD and the first RAD member failed to provide a fulsome review of all of the evidence that supported their conclusions.

propositions.text: RPD was correct to find Mr. XXXX is neither Convention refugee nor person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: Upon my full review of the evidence, I find that the RPD was correct to find that Mr. XXXX is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.

propositions.text: RPD was correct in concluding Mr. XXXX has viable internal flight alternative in New Delhi, Mumbai, and Calcutta.
propositions.quote: Specifically, I find that the RPD was correct in concluding that Mr. XXXX would have a viable internal flight alternative in New Delhi, Mumbai, and Calcutta.

propositions.text: I have carefully considered the Federal Court's judicial review findings in reaching this conclusion.
propositions.quote: In reaching this conclusion, I have had careful regard to the Court's findings on judicial review.

propositions.text: I provide detailed reasons and evidence references explaining why Mr. XXXX failed to establish no viable internal flight alternative.
propositions.quote: Below, I provide more detailed reasons and references to the evidence, to explain why Mr. XXXX has failed to establish that he would not have a viable internal flight alternative in New Delhi, Mumbai and/or Calcutta.

paragraphs.summary: The court reviews all evidence, finds RPD erred relying on parents' opinion, but agrees RPD was correct on internal flight alternative.

propositions.text: On October 2, 2020, I advised counsel of updated National Documentation Package (NDP) for India and invited submissions on internal flight alternative.
propositions.quote: By notice dated October 2, 2020, I advised Mr. XXXX counsel that the National Documentation Package (NDP) for India was updated on July 17, 2020. I provided Counsel with the opportunity to make submissions in relation to the new NDP for India, especially Tab 10.13 which addresses police databases and criminal tracking including the relationship with the Aadhar systems and tenant verification.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX counsel responded with fulsome submissions on internal flight alternative considering new NDP evidence.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX counsel responded to the RAD's notice by letter dated XXXX XXXX, 2020, in which she made fulsome submissions on the issue of internal flight alternative taking into account the evidence contained in the most recent NDP for India.

paragraphs.summary: The court invited and received new submissions from counsel on internal flight alternative based on updated NDP evidence.

propositions.text: I accept new submissions as they meet RAD Rules conditions and respond to my notice on internal flight alternative.
propositions.quote: I accept these new submissions as they meet the conditions set out in Rule 29 of the RAD Rules since the new submissions respond to my notice on the internal flight alternative issue. Therefore, they could not reasonably have been filed with the appeal record.

propositions.text: I will address counsel's submissions below.
propositions.quote: I address Counsel's submissions below.

paragraphs.summary: The court accepts new submissions as compliant and will address them below.

propositions.text: Onus is on Mr. XXXX to prove no viable internal flight alternative in India.
propositions.quote: The onus is on Mr. XXXX to demonstrate that he does not have a viable internal flight alternative in India.

propositions.text: Two-pronged test for internal flight alternative: (1) balance of probabilities no serious persecution or harm; (2) conditions not unreasonable to seek refuge there.
propositions.quote: The two-pronged test to establish an internal flight alternative is the following. (1) The decision maker must be satisfied on the balance of probabilities that the appellant would not face a serious possibility of persecution in the internal flight alternative location or a likelihood that he would be subjected personally to one of the types of harm that would make him a person in need of protection there. (2) The conditions in the part of the country under consideration must be such that it would not be unreasonable, in all the circumstances, for the appellant to seek refuge there.

propositions.text: Threshold for unreasonableness is very high, requiring conditions jeopardizing life and safety.
propositions.quote: The threshold for unreasonableness is a very high one and requires nothing less than the existence of conditions that would jeopardize the life and safety of a claimant.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the onus and two-pronged test for internal flight alternative, with a high threshold for unreasonableness.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD erred in finding no serious possibility of persecution in internal flight cities.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX counsel argues that the RPD erred in finding that Mr. XXXX would not face a serious possibility of persecution in New Delhi, Mumbai and Calcutta.

propositions.text: Counsel argues serious allegations suggest police might search for Mr. XXXX.
propositions.quote: In her appeal submissions, Counsel argues that the serious allegations against Mr. XXXX suggested that the police might carry out a search for him.

propositions.text: Counsel clarifies not arguing police would conduct complex interstate search.
propositions.quote: However, she also stated that she was not arguing that Mr. XXXX profile was significant enough for the police to carry out a complex interstate search for him.

propositions.text: Counsel argues Indian authorities have tools to find him and likely would track him down to extort or persecute.
propositions.quote: Instead, Counsel argued that, in light of the evidence on the tenant registration system and the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS), the Indian authorities would have all the tools necessary to find him and, given their past actions, they would more likely than not track him down to either extort money from him or to persecute him.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues RPD erred; police might track Mr. XXXX using tenant registration and CCTNS to extort or persecute him.

propositions.text: I disagree; Mr. XXXX has not established serious possibility police or brother would track and persecute him in internal flight cities.
propositions.quote: I disagree with this argument. Based on my own independent review of the evidence in this case against the background of the most recent NDP for India, I find that Mr. XXXX has not established a serious possibility that, if he returns to India, either the police from his district in Punjab or his former fiancée's brother would track him down and persecute him in New Delhi, Mumbai or Calcutta.

paragraphs.summary: The court disagrees with counsel and finds no serious possibility police or brother would track and persecute Mr. XXXX in internal flight cities.

propositions.text: RPD and first RAD decision lacked comprehensive review of evidence supporting conclusions on local nature of problems and lack of police/brother interest beyond local area.
propositions.quote: In my view, neither the RPD's decision nor the first RAD decision set out a sufficiently comprehensive review of the evidence that supported their conclusion that Mr. XXXX had failed to establish that his problems with the brother and the police extended beyond being a local matter. The RPD also failed to detail all of the evidence that supports the conclusion that Mr. XXXX failed to establish that the brother and/or the police from his district continue to have the kind of interest or motivation to search for him all over India, specifically in New Delhi, Mumbai, or Calcutta.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD and first RAD decisions lacked comprehensive evidence review on local nature of threats and police/brother interest.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX testified he has no family in internal flight cities and fears tenant registration would alert local police to Punjab police.
propositions.quote: When the RPD asked Mr. XXXX why he would not be able to safely relocate to New Delhi, Mumbai or Calcutta, he replied that he has no family in those cities. He then pointed to the tenant registration system and said that, if he relocated to one of the proposed internal flight alternative cities proposed by the RPD, the police in that city would contact the local police in his district in Punjab who would learn of his whereabouts in one of the three internal flight alternative cities.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX did not allege police or brother would conduct country-wide search for him.
propositions.quote: It is important to note that Mr. XXXX himself did not allege that the Punjabi police and/or his fiancée's brother would carry out a country-wide search for him.

propositions.text: Counsel corrected RPD that Mr. XXXX did not testify police would follow him to internal flight cities.
propositions.quote: In fact, when the RPD asked Mr. XXXX why, at the time of the hearing in 2017, he believed the police would follow him to the proposed internal flight alternative cities, his counsel pointedly corrected the RPD member saying that this was not his testimony and that he had not said the police would follow him to the internal flight alternative locations.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. XXXX testified no family in internal flight cities; fears tenant registration alerting Punjab police; did not allege country-wide police search.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX testified police harassed his parents, asked for money, arrested father once; brother harassed parents in 2016.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX replied that the police went to his parents' home and harassed them. ... said that the police asked his parents for money every 3-4 months and arrested his father once. He also added that his former fiancée's brother had harassed his parents when he saw them on the road one day in XXXX 2016.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX has not submitted new evidence of additional problems experienced by parents from police or brother.
propositions.quote: Despite being represented by the same counsel throughout these proceedings, Mr. XXXX has not submitted any new evidence raising any additional problems being experienced by his parents at the hands of the police or his former fiancée's brother.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. XXXX testified police and brother harassed parents; no new evidence submitted of further problems.

propositions.text: I disagree with counsel that Mr. XXXX would likely come to Punjab police attention through tenant registration process.
propositions.quote: Having reviewed the most recent NDP for India dated July 17, 2020, I disagree with Counsel that Mr. XXXX likely would come to the attention of the Punjab police through the tenant registration process.

paragraphs.summary: The court disagrees with counsel that tenant registration would alert Punjab police to Mr. XXXX.

propositions.text: India has no national police force; each state has separate police; minimal interstate communication except for major crimes.
propositions.quote: To begin, the documentary evidence found in the NDP for India continues to indicate that there is no national police force in India. Each state in India has a separate police force and there is minimal interstate police communication except in cases of major and high-profile crime.

propositions.text: NDP research report indicates no centralized registration system for police to check inhabitants' whereabouts within or across states.
propositions.quote: The new research report found at Tab 10.13 of the NDP cites sources who indicate that there is no centralized registration system in place to enable police to check the whereabouts of inhabitants in their own state, let alone in other states.

propositions.text: Police systems between districts and states are not integrated, creating 'islands of technology' communicating only within state or district.
propositions.quote: Another source cited in the report indicates that police systems between districts and states are not integrated thus creating "islands of technology" which can only communicate within a state or district.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds India has no national police, minimal interstate communication, and no centralized registration system.

propositions.text: Tenant registration laws exist but verification with home state police is very limited due to migrant volume.
propositions.quote: While India does have laws requiring the registration of new tenants, the most recent evidence in the NDP for India indicates that the actual verification of tenant backgrounds with the police in their home state is very limited.

propositions.text: Professor states tenant verification is 'extremely limited' due to migrant workers.
propositions.quote: A professor of criminal justice quoted in the research report indicated that, since a national Indian database does not exist, tenant verification is "extremely limited" due to the volume of workers who have migrated to large cities.

propositions.text: Former Delhi police commissioner states tenant verification is done for psychological satisfaction, no actual background check or follow-up with other states.
propositions.quote: The research report also reproduces a quote from a former deputy Delhi commissioner of police in an India Today article in which they stated that tenant verification is "done for the psychological satisfaction, nor for actual background check.... The cops don't make any effort to follow up with the concerned police station of other states."

paragraphs.summary: Tenant verification is legally required but practically limited and done mainly for psychological satisfaction, with no real background checks.

propositions.text: Prefers professor and former police commissioner evidence over anonymous officer's claim of some inter-state tenant info exchange.
propositions.quote: However, I prefer the information set out above from the professor of criminal justice and the former Delhi police commissioner of police over the anonymous Station House Officer quoted in the Indian Express article.

propositions.text: Information indicates tenant background checks with police from other states are 'extremely limited.'
propositions.quote: This information indicates that tenant background checks with police from other states are "extremely limited."

paragraphs.summary: The court prefers expert evidence indicating tenant background checks across states are extremely limited over anonymous contrary claims.

propositions.text: Evidence does not establish likelihood Mr. XXXX would come to Punjab police attention via tenant registration if relocated to internal flight cities.
propositions.quote: Based on a weighing of all of the evidence in the NDP for India, including the most recent evidence in Tab 10.3, I find that that the evidence does not establish a likelihood that Mr. XXXX would come to the attention of the Punjab police through the tenant registration system if he relocated to New Delhi, Mumbai or Calcutta.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no likelihood Mr. XXXX would be detected by Punjab police through tenant registration in internal flight cities.

propositions.text: Counsel argues Indian authorities have tools to find Mr. XXXX and likely would track him down to extort or persecute him.
propositions.quote: Counsel stated that she was not arguing that Mr. XXXX's profile was significant enough for the police to carry out a complex interstate search for him. Instead, Counsel argued that, in light of the evidence on the tenant registration system and the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS), the Indian authorities would have all the tools necessary to find him and, given the serious allegations of XXXX and XXXX made against him.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues Indian authorities have tools to find and likely track Mr. XXXX to extort or persecute him.

propositions.text: Police from Mr. XXXX's district or the brother of his former fiancée lack motivation to track him across India today.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with Counsel that the evidence establishes that the police from Mr. XXXX's district or the brother of Mr. XXXX's former fiancée have the kind of interest or motivation to expend the resources and effort to track Mr. XXXX down if he were to return to India today and relocate to New Delhi, Mumbai or Calcutta.

propositions.text: NDP evidence shows police stations are connected via CCTNS but interstate police communication is limited to major cases.
propositions.quote: While the evidence in the NDP indicates that there is increasing evidence that police stations are connected through the CCTNS, as noted above, the evidence in the NDP also indicates that there is little interstate police communication except for major cases like terrorism, or high-profile organized crime.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds police or the brother lack motivation to track Mr. XXXX across India; NDP shows limited interstate police communication except for major cases.

propositions.text: Brother of Mr. XXXX's fiancée had contact with police leading to false accusations and bribe release of Mr. XXXX.
propositions.quote: the brother appears to have told the police that Mr. XXXX was connected to XXXXs, which led the police to XXXX and XXXX Mr. XXXX... The police ended up releasing him on the payment of a bribe with a warning to stay away from his fiancée's family.

propositions.text: Brother has had no contact with Mr. XXXX's parents for five years and no evidence of harassment or pressure.
propositions.quote: There is no evidence that the brother has had any contact with Mr. XXXX's parents for the last five years, either to harass them, threaten them, or pressure them for information about Mr. XXXX's whereabouts.

propositions.text: No evidence brother knows Mr. XXXX's current location or has motivation to persecute him in internal flight locations.
propositions.quote: There was no evidence as to how the brother of Mr. XXXX's fiancée would even know that Mr. XXXX had returned to India and relocated to New Delhi, Mumbai or Calcutta now over five and a half years after he left India... little to no evidence that could support an inference that the brother of the fiancée has a continuing interest and motivation to take the steps that would be necessary to persecute or harm Mr. XXXX in any of the internal flight alternative locations.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the brother falsely accused Mr. XXXX, has had no contact or motivation to persecute him in internal flight locations for over five years.

propositions.text: Brother used local police contacts to harass Mr. XXXX before he left India but no ongoing interest to track him across India now.
propositions.quote: the evidence suggested that the brother of Mr. XXXX's fiancée had used his contacts within the local police to pressure them to locate Mr. XXXX to harass, detain and mistreat him before he left India. However, that does not mean that either the brother or the police continue to have the interest and motivation to track Mr. XXXX down all over India over six years after he left.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the brother used police to harass Mr. XXXX before but no ongoing interest to track him across India now.

propositions.text: No evidence police treated accusations seriously enough to search for Mr. XXXX across India; no charges or warrants exist.
propositions.quote: there was no evidence that the police were treating these accusations as the kind of serious case that would lead them to search for Mr. XXXX all over India... The police laid no formal charges against Mr. XXXX; there are no warrants for his arrest; there is no evidence that he is on a list of wanted persons or that the police from his district continue to actively search for him.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX passed Indian airport security using his personal passport without problems.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX was able to get through all of the security and immigration checks imposed at international airports in India without any problems using his own personal passport, which he filed with the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no evidence police seriously search for Mr. XXXX; he passed Indian airport security without issues.

propositions.text: Police harass Mr. XXXX's parents for money but visits insufficient to infer ongoing police interest to persecute Mr. XXXX.
propositions.quote: this evidence suggests that, unfortunately, the police are using Mr. XXXX's parents as a source of extra money by harassing them every now and then... such visits are insufficient to support an inference that the police have an ongoing interest and motivation to track down Mr. XXXX in another state in order to persecute or extort him.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds police harass Mr. XXXX's parents for money but lack ongoing interest to persecute Mr. XXXX.

propositions.text: Brother and police aimed to keep Mr. XXXX away from former fiancée's family; no evidence they would track him across India now.
propositions.quote: The available evidence would suggest that the motivation of the brother and the police was to ensure that Mr. XXXX had no further contact with his former fiancée and her family... Mr. XXXX has failed to meet his onus of establishing that either the brother or the police from his district has the interest and motivation to track him down all over India, and specifically in the internal flight alternative cities, if he were to relocate there today.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds brother and police wanted to keep Mr. XXXX away from former fiancée's family and lack motivation to track him across India now.

propositions.text: Central Monitoring System exists but no evidence it would be used to track Mr. XXXX in internal flight cities.
propositions.quote: I do not agree with counsel that the existence of a Central Monitoring System in India leads to a serious possibility that Mr. XXXX would be tracked down and persecuted in New Delhi, Mumbai or Calcutta... The evidence in this case did not establish that the Indian police would be likely to consider Mr. XXXX to be of such a high degree of interest that the government would undertake the steps necessary to review all the data in the Central Monitoring System in an attempt to track him down if he were to relocate to New Delhi, Mumbai, or Calcutta.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Central Monitoring System would not likely be used to track Mr. XXXX in internal flight cities.

propositions.text: RPD was correct that Mr. XXXX has not shown serious possibility of persecution if relocating to internal flight cities.
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD was correct to find that Mr. XXXX has not established that he would face a serious possibility of persecution or likelihood of serious harm if he relocates to New Delhi, Mumbai, or Calcutta for the more detailed reasons provided above.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the RPD was correct that Mr. XXXX has not shown serious risk if relocating to internal flight cities.

propositions.text: No argument that it would be unreasonable to expect Mr. XXXX to relocate to internal flight cities; he is a young man with factory work experience.
propositions.quote: Counsel has made no arguments as to why it would be unreasonable to expect Mr. XXXX to relocate to New Delhi, Mumbai, or Calcutta... Mr. XXXX is a young man who worked in a factory for several years before leaving India.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no argument against reasonableness of Mr. XXXX relocating to internal flight cities; he is young and worked in a factory.

propositions.text: Appeal dismissed; RPD decision confirmed that Mr. XXXX is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection.
propositions.quote: I dismiss the appeal and confirm the decision of the RPD that XXXX XXXX XXXX is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD decision that Mr. XXXX is not a refugee or in need of protection.
